questions.q: In Christian teaching, which of the following best describes the true meaning of 'Obedience'?
options: Doing whatever you feel is right at the moment
Willingly submitting to and carrying out the commands or instructions of an authority
Arguing with an instruction before eventually doing it
Following rules only when people are watching
questions.explain: **Obedience** is the act of willingly and promptly submitting to the instructions, laws, or commands given by God or any constituted authority.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Genesis 12:1-3, God called Abram (Abraham) to leave his country and kindred. What was one of the major blessings God promised him for his obedience?
options: He would become the richest man in Egypt.
God would make of him a great nation and bless him.
He would never face a famine in his life.
He would become a king over the entire earth.
questions.explain: **Genesis 12:2** says: 'And **I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you** and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.'
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to Genesis 12, Abraham demonstrated his obedience to God's call by leaving Haran at the age of ____________.
options: 50 years
75 years
90 years
100 years
questions.explain: **Genesis 12:4** records: 'Abram was **seventy-five years old** when he departed from Haran.'

questions.q: In Genesis 21:1-8, Abraham obeyed God regarding the birth of his promised son, Isaac, by doing what on the eighth day?
options: Offering him as a burnt offering
Dedicating him in the temple at Jerusalem
Circumcising him as God had commanded
Sending him away with Hagar
questions.explain: **Genesis 21:4** states: 'And Abraham **circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old**, as God had commanded him.'
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: God gave Abraham a very difficult test of obedience in Genesis 22:1-19. What did God ask him to do?
options: To go to war against five kings
To give all his wealth to the poor
To take his only son, Isaac, and offer him as a burnt offering
To leave his wife Sarah and marry another woman
questions.explain: In **Genesis 22:2**, God tested Abraham by commanding him: 'Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love... and **offer him there as a burnt offering**.'
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To which land did God instruct Abraham to go to sacrifice Isaac?
options: The land of Moriah
The land of Egypt
The land of Canaan
The land of Goshen
questions.explain: **Genesis 22:2** says: 'Go to the **land of Moriah**, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I shall tell you.'
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: As Abraham was about to slay Isaac in obedience to God's command, an angel of the Lord stopped him. What did God provide as a substitute for the sacrifice?
options: A dove sitting in a tree
A young bull grazing nearby
A ram caught in a thicket by its horns
A lamb sleeping on a rock
questions.explain: According to **Genesis 22:13**, Abraham looked up and saw 'a **ram, caught in a thicket by his horns**', which he took and offered as a burnt offering instead of his son.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)

questions.q: Because Abraham passed the ultimate test of obedience regarding Isaac, God swore an oath saying, 'in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because ____________.' (Genesis 22:18)
options: you have built an altar
you have obeyed my voice
you are a wealthy man
Isaac was a strong boy
questions.explain: **Genesis 22:18** concludes the blessing by stating: '...and in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, **because you have obeyed my voice**.'
